data.title: Real use case: Block orchestrates code migrations
data.summary: A named customer describes coordinating many pull requests while retaining human production controls.

sources.title: How Block orchestrates Claude Fable across thousands of pull requests

facts.text: In an October 8 provider interview, Block describes using frontier-model orchestration and smaller worker models for large code migrations, with people steering design and controlling releases.

prerequisites: Identify the intended host, task, source data and existing access.
steps: Read the customer account as a description of its own architecture and controls.
Choose a representative local migration slice and define behavior-preservation checks.
Compare pilot results and operating cost before deciding whether orchestration is warranted.
data.output: A bounded pilot design informed by a customer account.
validation: Reported scale is clearly attributed to Block.
Local performance and savings are measured separately if the pilot is later run.
limitations: Provider-published customer interview, not independent evidence. Block’s infrastructure and results were not reproduced; no ROI claim is made.
